Hi Alice — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the right pilot: 

Summary (what I heard)
- Primary requirement: customer data (PHI-adjacent telemetry) must not egress to any third-party network or region outside the US.
- Preference: isolated tenancy and customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest.
- Timeline: interested in a 6–8 week POC with production gating based on audit log access and penetration-test results.

Open items (next for Redwood)
1) Can we confirm whether "no egress" means: (a) no packet-level egress from the customer VPC at all, or (b) no copy of raw data stored outside the VPC / disks?
2) Do you require an HSM-backed KMS (customer-controlled) or is a customer-managed KMS in the cloud acceptable?
3) Preferred pilot environment: Dedicated capacity (Redwood-managed GPUs in a customer-dedicated VPC) vs Private (Redwood control plane in your VPC / on-prem). Any preference we should prioritize?

Proposed next steps
- Ben (SE) and I will put together a short ops diagram + checklist (network, firewall rules, KMS config) and share a draft SOW for the pilot.
- If helpful, we can schedule a technical deep-dive early next week to map network flows and identify any procurement/security blockers.

If you can reply with the answers to the three items above (especially #1), we'll shape the checklist and propose exact POC dates.

Thanks — looking forward.

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

Answers to your questions
1) No egress = no packet-level egress. All inference calls must terminate inside our VPC; we cannot allow outbound network connectivity to an external Redwood-managed network that could route tokens or raw telemetry outside the VPC.
2) Customer-managed KMS in our cloud account (AWS KMS with customer CMKs) is acceptable; we prefer an HSM-backed key but can start with customer-managed KMS if needed to expedite the POC.
3) Preference: Dedicated capacity in our VPC (we want Redwood-managed inference nodes that run in our VPC with strict VPC controls). If that proves infeasible for any reason, we might consider Private (Redwood control plane in our VPC or on-prem) but that is a heavier lift.

Other asks
- We need audit logs (both request-level and node-level) shipped to our S3 (or pushed to our Splunk) for the POC.
- Can you share a short runbook that shows how key material is provisioned and revoked during the pilot?

Jonas / Marissa — thanks. Short answer: yes, we can meet the requirements; below is an ops-level plan and the tradeoffs.

Feasibility summary
- Dedicated nodes placed into the customer's VPC (we call this “Dedicated in Customer VPC”) can be configured so there is no egress to any Redwood-managed public network. That is achieved by:
  - Deploying GPUs on instances with ENIs in the customer VPC and no internet gateway attachment on those subnets.
  - Requiring explicit VPC endpoints for any ancillary services (e.g., S3 or KMS) and restricting route tables so that outbound traffic is not permitted to the public internet.
  - Using AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering for control-plane telemetry channels; control plane can run in Redwood's control plane region but telemetry is routed over the peer/PrivateLink and terminated inside the customer's account.

KMS / key management
- We support customer CMKs (AWS KMS) and can integrate with HSM-backed keys. The recommended flow is: customer creates CMK and grants Redwood's service principal an Encrypt/Decrypt grant scoped to the pilot. Key rotation and revocation are documented in the checklist.

Audit logs and artifacts
- We can stream node logs and request traces to a customer S3 bucket (or push to Splunk via Kinesis/Firehose) without retaining raw payloads outside the VPC. We'll include the log delivery config in the ops checklist.

Tradeoffs & recommendation
- Dedicated-in-Customer-VPC: fastest path to a POC (minimal infra changes on your side beyond subnet/ENI setup + KMS grants). Meets the "no packet egress" requirement when properly configured.
- Private (Redwood control plane in-customer VPC / on-prem): heavier operational lift but gives the customer full control over the control plane. Consider this if you want long-term separation of the control plane.

Proposed next steps
1) Architecture call (30–45m) to walk the network diagram and confirm exact subnet/route/NAT constraints.
2) We will share: vpc-ops-checklist.pdf (network + KMS + logging steps) and draft-sow-template.docx for the 6–8 week pilot.
3) Ben + Jonas will present the architecture to OpenHealth Security (please confirm availability).

I attached the ops checklist and a draft SOW template to this message. If that looks good we can propose Wed/Thu next week for the architecture call.
